name: Markup Calculator
description: Calculate a selling price from cost and a target markup percentage, or find the markup applied between a cost and selling price you already know.

faq.question: Is markup the same as margin?
faq.answer: No. Markup is profit divided by cost; margin is profit divided by selling price. A 50% markup on a $40 item prices it at $60 — but that $20 profit is only a 33.3% margin, since margin divides by the larger selling price instead of the smaller cost. See the Profit Margin Calculator for the margin-first version of this math.

faq.question: Why would I use markup instead of margin for pricing?
faq.answer: Cost-plus pricing ("charge X% more than what I paid") is a very common retail and wholesale strategy, and markup is the natural percentage for that workflow since you're starting from a known cost. Margin is more useful when you're working backward from a target profitability percentage of revenue, which is how most financial reporting talks about profitability.
